initial_cache_backed_observation.comparison: Slower than the earlier Core library observation of 175.04 seconds. This prompted the interleaved wrapper-disabled controls below instead of a performance claim.

paired_control.method: Reuse a private target per arm, remove only the native package's reproducible outputs through Cargo clean before each build, and compile the unchanged exact source revision. Both arms use identical diagnostic flags and capacity leases. No cache hardlink is modified in place.

interpretation: The large initial slowdown did not repeat in the paired controls. The final warm command walls and native compiler units are essentially unchanged, so this foundation cut establishes physical ownership and independent test compilation without establishing a CI wall-time improvement. Most provider, agent-session, and orchestration code remains native.
limitations: Two interleaved observations per source on a shared host, not a latency distribution. The first pair rebuilds additional dependencies after the wrapper/diagnostic configuration change; its command walls are not native-only timings.
The wrapper-disabled controls change diagnostic and cache settings relative to the initial observation. They do not establish that Kache caused the initial slowdown.
This builds the default native library without otel, not the full shared CLI producer or its test units. Canonical CLI cache measurements are recorded separately.
The diagnostic flag is confined to this experiment. Production compiler flags and stack-frame budgets are unchanged.
The owning CI report still measures 1217.4-second p90 against 600, before these unlanded changes.
